question: Which cryptographic technique uses a single key for both encryption and decryption of data?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Symmetric encryption**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Symmetric encryption**, also known as **secret key encryption**.
 
• It involves the use of the **same cryptographic key for both the encryption of plaintext and the decryption of ciphertext.**
 
• The keys can either be identical or there may be a simple transformation to transition between the two keys.
 
• Simple symmetric encryption techniques include the** Caesar Cipher,** though this is typically considered easy to decipher with modern computational capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hashing**

 
 
• Hashing is a technique that converts an input of any length into a fixed-size string of text, using a mathematical function.
 
• It is primarily used for data integrity, not for encryption, and it is typically a one-way function, meaning the original data cannot be retrieved from the hash.
 
 
 
• **Public-key encryption**
 
 
• It is also known as asymmetric encryption.
 
• This type of encryption uses a pair of keys - one private and one public.
 
• The public key is used for encryption and the private key is used for decryption.
 
• It is primarily used in scenarios where secure data transmission is required over an insecure network like the Internet.
 
 
 
• **Asymmetric encryption**
 
 
• This is another name for public-key encryption.
 
• It uses two keys, one private and one public, for the encryption and decryption process.
 
• It offers high levels of security but requires greater computational resources than symmetric encryption.
